rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is directed to the Prophet while intending his community, or to anyone fit to receive it.
rows.anchor: الخطاب للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم والمراد به أمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فتقعد is subjunctive as a prohibition.
rows.anchor: بالنصب على النهي والقعود قيل بمعنى المكث

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some explain قعد as remaining or dwelling in a bad state, whether standing or sitting.
rows.anchor: قيل بمعنى المكث كما تقول هو قاعد في أسوأ حال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take قعد to mean becoming, as in the Arab expression for a blade that became spear-like.
rows.anchor: شحذ الشفرة حتى قعدت كأنها حربة أي صارت

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan objects that قعد meaning became is only attested in this fixed example and does not generally recur.
rows.anchor: وتعقب هذا أبو حيان بأن مجيء قعد بمعنى صار مقصور عند الأصحاب على هذا المثل

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farra allows قعد meaning became productively and treats the cited rajaz line accordingly, but al-Alusi says it is no proof.
rows.anchor: فإنه كما قال أبو حيان وغيره يقول باطراد ذلك وجعل منه قول الراجز

rows.speaker: الكسائي
rows.claim: Al-Kisa'i reports the expression قعد لا يسأل حاجة إلا قضاها, used this way by Baghdad speakers.
rows.anchor: وحكى الكسائي قعد لا يسأل حاجة إلا قضاها واستعمال البغداديين على هذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The incapacity sense is explained either metaphorically from sitting instead of standing, or as an allusion to the helpless person who sits down.
rows.anchor: فقيل هو مجاز من القعود ضد القيام كالمقعد بمعنى العاجز عن القيام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If قعود means incapacity here, its omitted complement is incapacity to attain the intended success.
rows.anchor: وإذا جعل القعود هنا بمعنى العجز فالفعل لازم متعلقة محذوف أي فتعجز عن الفوز بالمقصود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مذموما مخذولا can be the predicate of تقعد or two successive circumstantial descriptions.
rows.anchor: إما خبر أن لتقعد على القول الأخير وإما حالان مترادفان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheist incurs God's abandonment and blame from angels, believers, and rational people for making a needy creature God's partner.
rows.anchor: جامعا على نفسك الخذلان من الله تعالى والذم من الملائكة والمؤمنين

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan allows literal sitting: the blamed and abandoned person characteristically sits bewildered and reflective.
rows.anchor: وجوز أبو حيان أن يراد بالقعود حقيقته لأن من شأن المذموم المخذول أن يقعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse implies that a monotheist combines praise with divine support.
rows.anchor: وفي الآية إشعار بأن الموحد جامع بين المدح والنصرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas explains قضى as God commanded, in a report transmitted through Ali ibn Abi Talha.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس أنه قال : أي أمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On one parsing, أن is a مصدرية with an omitted preceding باء, while لا negates and conveys prohibition.
rows.anchor: على أن أن مصدرية والجار قبلها مقدر ولا نافية والمراد النهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parsings make أن prohibitive or explanatory after an implied saying; a weakened أن and other analyses are also proposed.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن تكون ناهية كما مر ولا ينافيه التأويل بالمصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proposal that لا is extra and the command means to worship God is rejected because the exception construction resists it.
rows.anchor: المعنى ألزم ربك عبادته وفيه أن الاستثناء يأبى ذلك

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari glosses قضى as issuing a command settled beyond possibility of repeal, often analyzed as semantic تضمين.
rows.anchor: في الكشاف تفسير قضى بأمر أمرا مقطوعا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A debate asks whether this decisive command would imply no one ever worships another god, requiring the address to be restricted to believers.
rows.anchor: وإلا لزم أن لا يعبد أحد غير الله تعالى فيحتاج إلى تخصيص الخطاب بالمؤمنين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection does not apply if قضى means its lexical sense of decisively settling; Ibn Abbas is also reported to say this entails no shirk if it means decree.
rows.anchor: أما لو أريد به معناه اللغوي الذي هو البت والقطع المشار إليه فلا يرد ما ذكره

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the original wording was ووصى ربك; the two waw letters joined and the public reading became وقضى ربك.
rows.anchor: ادعاه ابن عباس فيما يروى للقضاء من غير تفصيل

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In that report, Ibn Abbas says that if the wording had been decree, no one would have committed shirk.
rows.anchor: ولو نزلت على القضاء ما أشرك به أحد

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير والضحاك
rows.claim: A similar original-reading report is attributed by routes through Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Dahhak.
rows.anchor: من طريق سعيد بن جبير وابن أبي حاتم من طريق الضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب
rows.claim: The reading ووصى ربك is also reported from Ibn Mas'ud and Ubayy ibn Ka'b.
rows.anchor: ورويت هذه القراءة عن ابن مسعود وأبي بن كعب رضي الله تعالى عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi calls the report curious if sound, since interpreting قضى as a command removes the difficulty and is also reported from Ibn Abbas.
rows.anchor: وهذا إن صح عجيب من ابن عباس لاندفاع المحذور بحمل القضاء على الأمر

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines قضى as concluding a matter by speech or action, whether divine or human, and cites this verse as divine speech.
rows.anchor: في مفردات الراغب القضاء فصل الأمر قولا كان أو فعلا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command can mean a general request, including abandoning other worship; alternatively worshipping God alone is commanded by implication, with clearing away shirk first.
rows.anchor: إن معنى لا تعبدوا غيره اعبدوه وحده فهو أمر باعتبار لازمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only God merits worship, the utmost reverence, because only the supremely great benefactor possesses ultimate greatness and gives immense blessings.
rows.anchor: لأن العبادة غاية التعظيم وهي لا تليق إلا لمن كان في غاية العظمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This command and the good deeds that follow are presented as capital for striving toward the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وهذا وما عطف عليه من الأعمال الحسنة كالتفضيل للسعي للآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وبالوالدين إحسانا means to treat both parents well, either by supplying an omitted verb or by construing the phrase with a verb.
rows.anchor: أي وبأن تحسنوا بهما أو أحسنوا بهما إحسانا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari attaches the prepositional phrase to an omitted verb, since a genitive complement of a verbal noun cannot precede it.
rows.anchor: وهو الذي ذهب إليه الزمخشري ومنع تعلقه بالمصدر لأن صلته لا تتقدم عليه

rows.speaker: الواحدي
rows.claim: Al-Wahidi attaches the phrase to the verbal noun; al-Halabi distinguishes this from the omitted-verb analysis.
rows.anchor: وعلقه الواحدي به فقال الحلبي :

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Many grammarians permit a verbal noun's governed element to precede it when it is a ظرف or جار ومجرور, due to their breadth.
rows.anchor: ومذهب الكثير من النحاة جواز تقديم معموله إذا كان ظرفا مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إما is إن الشرطية plus an added ما that reinforces it.
rows.anchor: إما مركبة من إن الشرطية وما المزيدة لتأكيدهما

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says added ما permits the emphatic nūn on the verb; Abu Ishaq requires it, while Sibawayh reportedly does not.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري : ولذا صح لحوق النون المؤكدة للفعل

rows.speaker: أبو حية النميري وابن دريد
rows.claim: Abu Hayya al-Numayri and Ibn Durayd supply poetic examples showing that the emphatic nūn need not be obligatory after added ما.
rows.anchor: ويستشهد بقوله أبي حية النميري : فإما ترى لمتى هكذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read يبلغان in the dual; al-Zamakhshari makes أحدهما an appositive to the dual alif.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي ( إما يبلغان )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apposition analysis is challenged because the أكلوني البراغيث construction requires a dual verb or, under a disputed allowance, coordination with waw.
rows.anchor: بأن ذلك مشروط بأن يسند الفعل المثنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Critics say أحدهما would be partitive apposition, while كلاهما as a whole apposition adds nothing and creates an unattested coordination.
rows.anchor: بأن ( أحدهما ) على ذلك بدل بعض من كل لا كل من كل

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya proposes تقسيم apposition, comparing it to a poet's image of one sound leg and another crippled by fate.
rows.anchor: كما قاله ابن عطية فهو كقوله : فكنت كذي رجلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That analogy fails because this apposition lacks the required waw and the antecedent can denote either part.
rows.anchor: وتعقب بأنه ليس من البدل المذكور لأنه شرطه العطف بالواو

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali al-Farisi makes أحدهما apposition to the dual pronoun and كلاهما its emphasis, but objections include incompatible apposition and emphasis.
rows.anchor: وعن أبي علي الفارسي أن ( أحدهما ) بدل من ضمير التثنية

rows.speaker: در المصون
rows.claim: Al-Durr al-Masun repairs the parse by making أحدهما partitive apposition, then supplying a dual verb whose subject كلاهما emphasizes it.
rows.anchor: قال في الدر المصون : لا بد من إصلاحه بأن يجعل أحدهما بدل بعض من كل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi prefers an omitted verb not attached to a dual pronoun, with كلاهما as its subject, avoiding the other objections.
rows.anchor: ولعل المختار إضمار فعل لم يتصل به ضمير التثنية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Singular address forms at عندك and after it prevent ambiguity and make the prohibition apply to every individual parent-child pair.
rows.anchor: للاحتراز عن التباس المراد وهو نهي كل أحد عن تأفيف والديه ونهرهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address is singular in ولا تجعل for emphasis and plural in ألا تعبدوا to suit the majesty of the decree.
rows.anchor: وذكر أنه وحد الخطاب في ( ولا تجعل ) للمبالغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: فلا تقل لهما applies whether one parent is alone or both are present; أف is an interjection or a noun meaning I am annoyed.
rows.anchor: أي لواحد منهما حالتي الانفراد والاجتماع ( أف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle أف has around forty forms; readings vary in case and tanwin but agree on its doubled fā.
rows.anchor: وفيه نحو من أربعين لغة والوارد من ذلك في القراآت سبع

rows.speaker: نافع وحفص
rows.claim: Nafi and Hafs read أف with kasra and tanwin, making the annoyance indefinite: any measure of irritation.
rows.anchor: فقرأ نافع وحفص بالكسر والتنوين وهو للتنكير

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir and Ibn Amir read أف with fatḥa and no tanwin.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير وابن عامر بالفتح دون تنوين

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو السمال وزيد بن علي وابن عباس
rows.claim: Other readings include Nafi with nominative tanwin, Abu al-Simal with ḍamma, Zayd ibn Ali with accusative tanwin, and Ibn Abbas with sukūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع في رواية عنه بالرفع والتنوين وأبو السمال بالضم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition covers showing irritation at what one finds unpleasant or burdensome in caring for parents.
rows.anchor: ومحصل المعنى لا تتضجر مما يستقذر منهما وتستثقل من مؤنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If forbidding أف implies all other harm by clear analogy, this is called mafhūm al-muwāfaqa, dalālat al-naṣṣ, or fahwā al-khiṭāb.
rows.anchor: ويسمى مفهوم الموافقة ودلالة النص وفحوى الخطاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view says the prohibition directly and conventionally forbids every kind of harm, like saying someone owns neither a tiny nor a large amount.
rows.anchor: وقيل يدل على ذلك حقيقة ومنطوقا في عرف اللغة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Nahr is separately prohibited because of its importance; it means harshly rebuking or stopping parents from what they do.
rows.anchor: وخص بعض أنواع الايذاء بالذكر في قوله تعالى ( ولا تنهرهما

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: The Imam distinguishes أف, forbidding any little or great display of annoyance, from نهر, forbidding verbal opposition that rebuts or accuses parents of lying.
rows.anchor: المراد من قوله تعالى ( ولا تقل لهما أف ) المنع من إظهار الضجر

rows.speaker: الإمام
rows.claim: On this distinction, mentioning نهر after أف is not redundant, and the order reflects their different harms.
rows.anchor: ولذا روعي هذا الترتيب وإلا فالمنع من التأفيف يدل على المنع من النهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قولا كريما is pleasant speech without harshness, appropriate to good manners and deference to parents.
rows.anchor: أي جميلا لا شراسة فيه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says whatever is distinguished in its category is called noble; some scholars take noble speech as arising from generosity and gentleness.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : كل شيء يشرف في بابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling parents father and mother rather than by their names is an example of proper speech, not an exhaustive definition.
rows.anchor: مثل أن يقول يا أبتاه ويا أماه ولا يدعوهما بأسمائهما

rows.speaker: زهير بن محمد
rows.claim: Zuhayr ibn Muhammad says that when parents call, one should answer لبيكما وسعديكما.
rows.anchor: عن زهير بن محمد أنه قال فيه : إذا دعواك فقل لبيكما وسعديكما

rows.speaker: أبو الهداج
rows.claim: Abu al-Haddaj asks Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib what noble speech means; Sa'id answers: the sinful servant's speech to a harsh master.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الهداج أنه قال : قلت لسعيد بن المسيب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lowering the wing of humility means being humble and submissive toward one's parents.
rows.anchor: أي تواضع لهما وتذلل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One analysis makes this one's humble wing, using the wing as a figure for humility and the lowering as its reinforcing image.
rows.anchor: على معنى جناحك الذليل ويكون ( جناح الذل )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another analysis makes a hidden metaphor of humility as a low-flying bird, imaginatively giving it wings and reinforcing the image by lowering them.
rows.anchor: قول لبيد : وغداة ريح قد كشفت وقرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A bird lowers and folds its wings when fearing a predator, a picture of extreme fear and abasement; lowering wings over chicks is another proposed image, apt to nurturing.
rows.anchor: وهي غاية خوفه وتذلله وقيل المراد بخفضهما ما يفعله إذا ضم فراخه للتربية

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf treats the phrase as an implicit metaphor that has become a figure for the utmost humility; its composite image resolves the objection that a raised wing would show more power.
rows.anchor: وفي الكشف أن في الكلام استعارة بالكناية ناشئة من جعل الجناح الذل

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Sa'id ibn Jubayr reads من الذل with kasra, meaning submission, a word originally used of animals; ḍamma is the human condition opposite honor.
rows.anchor: وقرأ سعيد بن جبير ( من الذل ) بكسر الذال وهو الانقياد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من الرحمة means from abundant compassion for them, with من marking source or cause.
rows.anchor: أي من فرط رحمتك عليهما فمن ابتدائية على سبيل التعليل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: من الرحمة cannot be explanatory apposition: the wing of humility is not itself mercy, though lowering it can be merciful.
rows.anchor: ولا يحتمل البيان حتى يقال لو كان كذا لرجعت الاستعارة إلى التشبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase magnifies humility by making all mercy its source; defining mercy as all mercy is another reported explanation that he rejects.
rows.anchor: واستفادة المبالغة من جعل جنس الرحمة مبدأ للتذلل

rows.speaker: الخفاجي
rows.claim: Al-Khafaji's verse illustrates the abasement of a ruler who becomes dependent on his own subordinate.
rows.anchor: يا من أتى يسأل عن فاقتي ما حال من يسأل من سائله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer asks God for lasting afterlife mercy rather than relying only on the child's transient kindness; it may also include both kinds of mercy.
rows.anchor: وادع الله تعالى أن يرحمهما برحمته الباقية وهي رحمة الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some restrict this prayer to Muslim parents; another view makes it general but abrogated by the prohibition on seeking forgiveness.
rows.anchor: قيل إنها مخصوصة بالأبوين المسلمين وقيل عامة منسوخة بآية النهي عن الاستغفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view keeps the prayer general without abrogation because the prohibition concerns after death while this supplication is before death; seeking faith for parents is merciful.
rows.anchor: وقيل عامة ولا نسخ لأن تلك الآية بعد الموت وهذه قبله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The claim that the verse was abrogated is transmitted from Ibn Abbas through several routes.
rows.anchor: من طرق عن ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كما ربياني compares the requested mercy to the parents' raising of the child, understood as mercy; another analysis pairs mercy and upbringing across both clauses.
rows.anchor: الكاف للتشبيه والجار والمجرور صفة مصدر مقدر أي رحمة مثل تربيتهما لي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading compares God's mercy with the parents' mercy, taking upbringing itself as mercy, or pairing both mercy and upbringing across the clauses.
rows.anchor: على أن التربية رحمة وجوز أن يكون لهما الرحمة والتربية معا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The continuation رب ارحمهما وربهما كما رحماني وربياني is judged remote as an interpretation of the paired mercy and upbringing.
rows.anchor: رب ارحمهما وربهما كما رحماني وربياني ( صغيرا 42 ( وفيه بعد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taking the comparative كاف as causal departs from its familiar meaning, while comparison already conveys the proposed sense.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن تكون الكاف للتعليل أي لأجل تربيتهما لي

rows.speaker: الطيبي
rows.claim: Al-Tibi reads the كاف as confirming the reality of the requested mercy, like a Qur'anic comparison in another verse.
rows.anchor: وقال الطيبي إن الكاف لتأكيد الوجود كأنه قيل رب ارحمهما رحمة محققة

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf calls al-Tibi's interpretation a good one.
rows.anchor: قال في الكشف وهو وجه حسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A temporal reading of ما that makes the parents' need occur at Judgment and the mercy mean Paradise is grammatically unsupported.
rows.anchor: وأما الحمل على أن ما المصدرية جعلت حينا أي ارحمهما في وقت أحوج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to pray for parents is apparently obligatory, and once suffices because a command does not itself entail repetition.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الأمر للوجوب فيجب على الولد أن يدعو لوالديه بالرحمة

rows.speaker: سفيان
rows.claim: Sufyan hopes that praying for parents in the final tashahhud is enough, by analogy with commanded blessings on the Prophet and remembrance during appointed days.
rows.anchor: وقد سئل سفيان كم يدعو الانسان لوالديه في اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God emphasizes parents by pairing kindness to them with monotheism and joining both in the divine decree.
rows.anchor: ولو لم يكن سوى أن شفع الإحسان إليهما بتوحيده سبحانه

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A sound report says God's pleasure is in the parents' pleasure and His anger in their anger; al-Hakim grades it sound on Muslim's criteria.
rows.anchor: رضا الله تعالى في رضا الوالدين وسخط الله تعالى في سخط الوالدين

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A man seeking permission to join jihad was told that caring for his living parents was his jihad.
rows.anchor: أحي والداك قال : نعم قال : ففيهما فجاهد

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says even the slightest thing below أف would have been forbidden, and contrasts the fate of disobedient and dutiful children.
rows.anchor: لو علم الله تعالى شيئا أدنى من الأف لنهى عنه

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar tells a man carrying his mother around the Kaaba that even one labor pain would not repay her, though God rewards good deeds greatly.
rows.anchor: يا ابن عمر أتراني جزيتها قال : لا ولا بطلقة واحدة

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A Muslim report says a child can repay a parent only by finding the parent enslaved, buying him, and freeing him.
rows.anchor: لا يجزي ولد والده إلا أن يجده مملوكا فيشتريه فيعتقه

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: A report from Jabir whose chain contains an unknown narrator says a father explains that he spent his son's money on family and himself, then recites a poem about raising him and receiving harshness.
rows.anchor: بسند فيه من لا يعرف عن جابر قال : جاء رجل

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: After the father's account, the Prophet rebukes the son and says that the son and his property belong to his father.
rows.anchor: فحينئذ أخذ النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بتلابيب ابنه وقال : أنت ومالك لأبيك

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Asked who most deserves good companionship, the Prophet names the mother three times and then the father; both canonical collections transmit it.
rows.anchor: قال : أمك قال : ثم من قال : أمك

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Filial duty continues after a parent's death through prayer, seeking forgiveness, honoring commitments, maintaining kinship ties, and honoring the parent's friends.
rows.anchor: الصلاة عليهما والاستغفار لهما وإيفاء عهدهما من بعدهما

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: Ibn Hibban's version adds that the listener calls this abundant and good, and is told to act on it.
rows.anchor: قال الرجل : ما أكثر هذا يا رسول الله وأطيبه

rows.speaker: أنس
rows.claim: Anas reports that someone whose parent dies while he has been disobedient can keep praying and seeking forgiveness until God records him as dutiful.
rows.anchor: إن العبد ليموت والداه أو أحدهما وإنه لهما لعاق فلا يزال يدعو لهما

rows.speaker: الأوزاعي
rows.claim: Al-Awza'i says a formerly disobedient child may become dutiful by settling parents' debts and praying for them, while a formerly dutiful one may be written disobedient for neglecting duties.
rows.anchor: بلغني أن من عق والديه في حياتهما ثم قضى دينا إن كان عليهما

rows.speaker: محمد بن النعمان
rows.claim: A report raised to the Prophet says visiting a parent's grave every Friday brings forgiveness and a record of dutifulness.
rows.anchor: من زار قبر أبويه أو أحدهما في كل جمعة غفر له وكتب برا

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn Umar honors a man because his father was a friend of Umar, citing the Prophet that filial piety maintains ties with a father's friends.
rows.anchor: إن أبر البر صلة الولد أهل ود أبيه

rows.speaker: أبو بردة
rows.claim: Abu Burda reports Ibn Umar saying whoever wants to maintain ties with his father in the grave should keep ties with his father's friends.
rows.anchor: من أحب أن يصل أباه في قبره فليصل إخوان أبيه من بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reports establish that disobedience to parents is among the gravest major sins, a point the scholars agree on.
rows.anchor: وصح عد العقوق من أكبر الكبائر وكونه منها هو ما اتفقوا عليه

rows.speaker: أكثر العلماء
rows.claim: Most scholars make no distinction between disobedience toward non-Muslim and Muslim parents; specifying Muslim parents in one report either stresses the worse case or the common case.
rows.anchor: وظاهر كلام الأكثرين بل صريحه أنه لا فرق في ذلك بين أن يكون الوالدان كافرين

rows.speaker: الحليمي
rows.claim: Al-Halimi's weak view grades disobedience as major if abusive, minor if it is only resentment while obeying, and major if the resentment harms parents by making them cease advising.
rows.anchor: وللحليمي ههنا تفصيل مبني على رأي له ضعيف وهو أن العقوق كبيرة

rows.speaker: البلقيني
rows.claim: Al-Bulqini defines disobedience to include harm that would be minor toward another but major toward a parent, or disobeying commands involving serious risk to the child.
rows.anchor: العقوق لأحد الوالدين هو أن يؤذيه بما لو فعله مع غيره كان محرما

rows.speaker: البلقيني
rows.claim: His definition also includes refusal of difficult non-obligatory travel or a long absence without beneficial learning or earning, and conduct likely to cause serious dishonor.
rows.anchor: أو في غيبة طويلة فيما ليس بعلم نافع ولا كسب فيه

rows.speaker: البلقيني
rows.claim: On this test, conduct that is a minor prohibited harm toward a stranger becomes major toward a parent; taking a trivial amount of a parent's money is excluded if it causes no hurt.
rows.anchor: وخرج بقولنا : أن يؤذي ما لو أخذ فلسا

rows.speaker: البلقيني
rows.claim: Taking a large amount that actually hurts a parent is major because the equivalent taking from someone else would already be a serious wrong.
rows.anchor: فإن أخذ مالا كثيرا بحيث يتأذى المأخوذ منه من الوالدين بذلك فإنه يكون

rows.speaker: البلقيني
rows.claim: Suing a parent for a debt may or may not be disobedience depending on whether imprisoning the parent is legally permissible and on the child's own legal belief.
rows.anchor: وأما الحبس فإن فرعناه على جواز حبس الوالد

rows.speaker: البلقيني
rows.claim: Nahr or أف is major if the same conduct is forbidden toward another; if it is not forbidden toward others, it is minor toward parents.
rows.anchor: وأما إذا نهر أحد والديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A lawful complaint or debt claim is not itself disobedience; a Companion's child complained to the Prophet without being rebuked.
rows.anchor: وأما مجرد الشكوى الجائزة والطلب الجائز فليس من العقوق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parental permission rule concerns jihad and similarly dangerous journeys where the child may lose life or limb and parents would grieve intensely.
rows.anchor: وقولنا أن يخالف أمره ونهيه فيما يدخل منه الخوف

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet tells a man seeking jihad to return to his living parents and strive by serving them; another narration tells him to make them laugh after making them cry.
rows.anchor: قال له : أحي والداك قال : نعم قال : ففيهما فجاهد

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Sa'id reports a migrant asked whether his parents in Yemen consented; the Prophet sends him back to seek permission and serve them if they refuse.
rows.anchor: قال : هل لك أحد باليمن قال : أبواي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A child need not seek permission for jihad and similar travel from a parent suspected of opposing Islam; where permission matters, free or enslaved status makes no difference.
rows.anchor: ما لم يتهم الولد في ذلك أخرجنا به ما لو كان الوالد كافرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Difficult voluntary pilgrimage requires parental permission, while obligatory pilgrimage does not; permission for sea travel despite likely safety is not clearly required.
rows.anchor: أردنا به السفر لحج التطوع حيث كان فيه مشقة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Travel for obligatory or communal learning is allowed when travel may bring focus or a teacher; without such expected benefit, permission is needed.
rows.anchor: وأما سفره للعلم المتعين أو لفرض الكفاية فلا منع منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A parent entitled to support can forbid travel that abandons that duty; travel that exposes the child to serious reputational suspicion can also be forbidden, especially for a woman.
rows.anchor: وحيث وجبت النفقة للوالد على الولد وكان في سفره تضييع للواجب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Disobeying advice that causes no harm is not disobedience, though following it is better.
rows.anchor: وأما مخالفة أمره ونهيه فيما لا يدخل على الولد فيه ضرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another scholar defines disobedience as causing parents nontrivial customary harm, while allowing excuse when an irrational parent's demand is not normally binding.
rows.anchor: أن العقوق فعل ما يحصل منه لهما أو لأحدهما إيذاء ليس بالهين عرفا

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: A man asks Abu al-Darda about his father demanding he divorce his beloved wife; Abu al-Darda declines to order either disobedience or divorce and cites the son as a gate of Paradise.
rows.anchor: إن أبي لم يزل بي حتى زوجني امرأة وأنه الآن يأمرني بفراقها

rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: In a hasan-sahih report, Ibn Umar refuses his father's order to divorce a beloved wife until the Prophet himself orders the divorce.
rows.anchor: كان تحتي امرأة أحبها وكان عمر يكرهها فقال لي طلقها فأبيت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A parent's command without a reasonable basis is not binding when sensible people see no harm in refusal; nontrivial customary harm is the sounder measure of disobedience.
rows.anchor: هذا هو الذي يتجه في تقرير الحد

rows.speaker: البلقيني
rows.claim: Al-Alusi objects to restricting disobedience to acts that would be minor sins toward nonparents, since serious customary harm may not be forbidden toward others.
rows.anchor: وتعقب ما نقل عن البلقيني بأن تخصيصه العقوق بفعل المحرم الصغيرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parents merit honor as the apparent cause of the child's existence and care; few others benefit the child as much.
rows.anchor: أنهما السبب الظاهري في إيجاده وتعيشه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A philosophical objection says parents sought sexual pleasure and brought the child into suffering; al-Alusi answers that their later care and protection outweigh that initial motive.
rows.anchor: إن الوالدين إنما طلبا تحصيل اللذة لأنفسهما فلزم منه دخول الولد في الوجود

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exposure to worldly suffering cannot cancel parents' rights, or it would cancel God's right as the true creator; suffering is also balanced by eternal bliss.
rows.anchor: لو كان الادخال في عالم الكون والفساد والتعريض للإكدار والإنكار دافعا لحق الوالدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alleged sage beat his father, arguing that the father exposed him to death, poverty, blindness, and disability by bringing him into the world.
rows.anchor: هو الذي أدخلني في عالم الكون والفساد وعرضني للموت والفقر

rows.speaker: أبو العلاء المعري
rows.claim: Asked what should be written on his grave, Abu al-Ala proposes a line blaming his father for his suffering while denying that he harmed anyone.
rows.anchor: هذا جناه أبي علي وما جنيت على أحد

rows.speaker: أبو العلاء المعري
rows.claim: Al-Ma'arri praises childlessness as the blessing of nonexistence that shields one from present and future suffering.
rows.anchor: وتركت فيهم نعمة العدم التي سبقت وصدت عن نعيم العاجل

rows.speaker: ابن رشيق
rows.claim: Ibn Rashiq's poem blames parents' pleasure for children's hardship and says existence brings suffering.
rows.anchor: قبح الله لذة لشقانا نالها الأمهات والآباء

rows.speaker: الإسكندر
rows.claim: Alexander reportedly says his teacher's sacrifices for education outweighed his father's pursuit of pleasure; al-Alusi answers that parental care after birth is greater.
rows.anchor: الأستاذ أعظم منه لأنه تحمل أنواع الشدائد والمحن عن تعليمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows the inner intention to honor parents, warning against hidden resentment and comforting those intending goodness.
rows.anchor: من قصد البر وانعقاد ما يجب من التوقير لهما

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf reads the verse as explaining the emphasis on parental kindness: God knows the inward state and repays it accordingly.
rows.anchor: بأن الله تعالى أعلم بما في ضمائرهم من ذلك فمجازيهم على حسبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse apparently promises reward to those intending good and warns others, while the promise predominates.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنه وعد لمن أضمر البر ووعيد لغيره لكن غلب ذلك الجانب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Being صالحين means intending righteousness and filial kindness rather than disobedience and corruption.
rows.anchor: قاصدين الصلاح والبر دون العقوق والفساد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الأوابين are those who return to God in repentance for lapses humans cannot wholly avoid; God forgives shortcomings and harm.
rows.anchor: أي الراجعين إليه تعالى التائبين عما فرط منهم مما لا يكاد يخلو من البشر

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf sees this as relief after a demanding warning: a rare, unintentional lapse by someone generally upright is met with divine care.
rows.anchor: تيسير بعد التأكيد والتعسير مع تضييق وتحذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr says the verse concerns an occasional lapse toward one's parents; it may also be general, with a repentant offender against parents especially included.
rows.anchor: وكون الآية في البادرة تكون من الرجل إلى والديه مروي عن ابن جبير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذَا القربى means a relative, and حقه is the right owed to that person.
rows.anchor: أي ذا القرابة منك ( حقه ( الثابت له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view means unmarriageable relatives and their right to support when poor and unable to earn, inferred from the parallel financial rights of the poor and traveler.
rows.anchor: قيل ولعل المراد بذي القربى المحارم وبحقهم النفقة عليهم إذا كانوا فقراء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some infer obligatory support for needy unmarriageable relatives who are neither parents nor children.
rows.anchor: واستدل بعضهم بالآية على إيجاب نفقة المحارم المحتاجين

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf says the right is general, including financial rights, maintaining ties, and good companionship, so the verse does not prove a specific support obligation.
rows.anchor: أن إيتاء الحق عام والمقام يقتضي الشمول فيتناول الحق المالي وغيره من الصلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi objects that حقه signals entitlement and, given the general wording, the verse can support a financial right; relatives are not limited to descendants.
rows.anchor: وتعقب أن قوله تعالى ( حقه ) يشعر باستحقاق ذلك

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi identifies ذي القربى as the Prophet's relatives, whose right is honor and a share of the fifth.
rows.anchor: وقيل : المراد بذي القربى أقارب الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: علي بن الحسين
rows.claim: Ali ibn al-Husayn tells a man from Syria that the Prophet's family are the relatives meant and their right is respect and the fifth.
rows.anchor: أخرج ابن جرير عن علي بن الحسين رضي الله تعالى عنهما أنه قال لرجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi says restricting the verse to the Prophet's kin lacks contextual evidence; treating the address itself as proof is unconvincing.
rows.anchor: وضعف بأنه لا قرينة على التخصيص وأجيب بأن الخطاب قرينة

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: A report says the Prophet gave Fatima Fadak when the verse was revealed, but al-Alusi doubts it because the sura is Meccan and Fadak was not then under the Prophet's control.
rows.anchor: من أنه لما نزلت هذه الآية دعا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فاطمة فأعطاها فدكا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tabdhir is spending wealth where it does not belong, pictured by scattering seed without tending where it lands.
rows.anchor: فإن التبذير إنفاق في غير موضعه مأخوذ من تفريق البذر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Mas'ud defines waste as spending money outside its proper right.
rows.anchor: عن ابن مسعود أنه قال : التبذير إنفاق المال في غير حقه

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Mawardi distinguishes excess by quantity from waste by wrong venue; both are blameworthy, and waste is worse.
rows.anchor: وفرق الماوردي بينه وبين الإسراف بأن الإسراف تجاوز في الكمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling squanderers brothers of devils explains the prohibition by linking them with the devil's company.
rows.anchor: تعليل للنهي عن التبذير ببيان أنه يجعل صاحبه ملزوزا في قرن الشياطين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إخوان may mean people resembling devils in bad traits, friends and followers in waste and sin, or companions destined for Hell.
rows.anchor: والمراد به الممائل مجازا أي أنهم مماثلون لهم في صفات السوء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Reported examples include slaughtering camels for gambling and wasting wealth for show or in forbidden amusements.
rows.anchor: فإنهم كانوا ينحرون الإبل ويتياسرون عليها ويبذرون أموالهم في السمعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The devil's kufr toward his Lord is extreme ingratitude: he turns every power from its created purpose toward sin, corruption, and misguidance.
rows.anchor: مبالغة في كفران نعمه تعالى لأن شأنه صرف جميع ما أعطاه الله تعالى من القوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming this trait signals that waste diverts God's blessings from their proper use, the opposite of gratitude; mentioning lordship hints at rebellion.
rows.anchor: وفي تخصيص هذا الوصف بالذكر من بين صفاته القبيحة إيذان بأن التبذير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some allow kufr here to mean the opposite of faith, but al-Alusi says that is not the sound reading.
rows.anchor: ويشعر كلام بعضهم بجواز حمل الكفر هنا على ما يقابل الإيمان وليس بذاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The most apparent object of turning away is the relatives, poor, and traveler just mentioned; another view makes them all petitioners.
rows.anchor: أي عن ذي القربى والمسكين وابن السبيل على ما هو الظاهر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning away literally means showing one's side; it is reported that the Prophet turned his face and fell silent when asked for something unavailable.
rows.anchor: بناء على ما روي من أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم كان إذا سئل شيئا ليس عنده صرف وجهه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address includes the Prophet and others; Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Dahhak explain the hoped-for mercy as provision.
rows.anchor: والخطاب عام له صلى الله عليه وسلم ولغيره والمراد بالرحمة على ما أخرج ابن جرير

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and al-Dahhak gloss the hoped-for mercy as provision; grammatically ابتغاء is a causal object.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك الرزق ونصب ( ابتغاء )

rows.speaker: الكشف
rows.claim: Al-Kashf says seeking provision stands in for lacking it: the effect is put for its cause, since the turn-away follows seeking resources.
rows.anchor: قد أقيم ابتغاء الرزق مقام فقدانه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other parses take ابتغاء as waiting for mercy, a circumstantial phrase, or attached to the conditional; attachment to the genitive pronoun is remote.
rows.anchor: وقد يفسر الإبتغاء بالإنتظار ويجوز جعله في موضع الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes turning away as inability to give and seeking as inability; a report about petitioners from Muzayna supports it, with mercy glossed as spoils.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون الإعراض كناية عن عدم النفع وترك الإعطاء لأنه لازمه عرفا

rows.speaker: عطاء الخراساني
rows.claim: Ata al-Khurasani reports that people from Muzayna asked the Prophet for mounts, left crying when he had none, and thought he was angry; the verse came down.
rows.anchor: عن عطاء الخراساني قال : جاء ناس من مزينة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Alusi doubts that historical application because the sura is Meccan and this verse is not an exception; a future conditional can account for the report's past-tense wording.
rows.anchor: إن هذا غير ظاهر بناء على ما سمعت من أن هذه السورة مكية

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari attaches ابتغاء to the response, meaning to speak gently when turning away in hope of mercy; the grammar is disputed.
rows.anchor: وقدم هذا الوجه على سائر الأوجه الزمخشري واعترض بأن ما بعد الفاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The post-fa phrase cannot ordinarily govern before it except under the Kufan allowance or through an implied semantic link; the euphemistic sense is not restricted to one parse.
rows.anchor: وأجيب بأنه ذكره على المذهب الكوفي المجوز للعمل مطلقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ترجوها can describe the mercy or be circumstantial for the person turning away; من ربك modifies ترجوها.
rows.anchor: وجملة ( ترجوها ) على سائر الأوجه يحتمل أن تكون وصفا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ميسورا is a passive participle meaning easy, so the response should be gentle speech and a gracious promise.
rows.anchor: والميسور اسم مفعول من يسر الأمر بالبناء للمجهول

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan says the gentle answer promises honor and help when resources arrive.
rows.anchor: قال الحسن : أمر أن يقول لهم نعم وكرامة

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the phrase as a prayer that God provide for both parties and bless them.
rows.anchor: وفسره ابن زيد برزقنا الله تعالى وإياكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another parse treats ميسور as a verbal noun, used intensively or with an omitted ذو, meaning a prayer for ease.
rows.anchor: وقيل الميسور مصدر وجعل صفة مبالغة أو بتقدير مضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source-noun analysis is less apparent, though its defenders say prayer for ease is called ميسر rather than ميسور.
rows.anchor: والحق أن اعتباره مصدرا خلاف الظاهر

rows.speaker: مالك
rows.claim: Imam Malik disliked telling an unserved petitioner رزقك الله because the petitioner may find it burdensome; al-Alusi calls this far-fetched.
rows.anchor: وعن الإمام مالك رحمه الله تعالى أنه كان لا يرى أن يقال للسائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse can imply that if one turns away one should still answer kindly, rather than ignore the petitioner.
rows.anchor: وأفاد بعضهم أن في الآية دليلا على النهي عن الإعراض

rows.speaker: العز بن عبد السلام
rows.claim: Al-Izz questions why hoped-for mercy conditions the gentle response, since a good answer is needed either way.
rows.anchor: واستشكل العز بن عبد السلام جعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The response reads the phrase as promising a gift only when there is hope of obtaining it; al-Alusi finds this unpersuasive.
rows.anchor: وأجاب بأن المراد بالقول الميسور الوعد بالعطاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This explains how to respond when lack of provision forces one to turn away: speak gently, since God controls provision.
rows.anchor: تعليل لقوله سبحانه ( وإما تعرضن عنهم )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God expands or constricts provision according to wisdom, so temporary hardship that prevents giving serves a purpose.
rows.anchor: وهو سبحانه يوسعه على بعض ويضيقه على بعض حسبما تتعلق به مشيئته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's knowledge of every servant's secret and needs explains His control of provision and reinforces the intervening call to moderation.
rows.anchor: بعباده ( جميعهم ( خبيرا ( عالما بسرهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively this grounds moderation because expansion and constriction belong to God, or because people should emulate God's measured distribution.
rows.anchor: وجوز أن يكون ذلك تعليلا للأمر بالقتصاد المستفاد من النهيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Applying the verse only to the last prohibition, meaning not to be miserly with those whose provision is restricted, is judged unsound.
rows.anchor: وجوز كونه تعليلا للنهي الأخير على معنى أنه تعالى يبسط ويقبض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One might make the preceding statement a lead-in to the child-killing prohibition, but al-Alusi says this is unlikely because the expected wording would differ.
rows.anchor: كونه تمهيدا لقوله سبحانه ﴿ ولا تقتلوا أولادكم خشية إملاق ﴾

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses إملاق as poverty; a cited line of Arabic poetry uses it in that sense.
rows.anchor: والإملاق الفقر كما روي عن ابن عباس وأنشد له قول الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent command forbids killing any children, male or female, for fear of poverty; a reported pre-Islamic practice specifically buried girls for fear of supporting them.
rows.anchor: وظاهر اللفظ النهي عن جميع أنواع قتل الأولاد ذكورا كانوا أو إناثا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The historical application takes الأولاد as daughters and killing as burial, since some pre-Islamic Arabs buried girls fearing they could not support them.
rows.anchor: روي أن من أهل الجاهلية من كان يئد البنات مخافة العجز عن النفقة عليهن

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines خشية as fear mixed with reverence, usually grounded in knowledge of what is feared.
rows.anchor: قال الراغب : وأكثر ما يكون ذلك عن علم بما يخشى منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word خشية is also read with kasra on its initial خاء.
rows.anchor: وقريء بكسر الخاء

rows.speaker: الطبرسي
rows.claim: Al-Tabarsi connects this prohibition to the earlier command لا تعبدوا إلا إياه, allowing the verb to be subjunctive with أن.
rows.anchor: عطفه على قوله سبحانه ( لا تعبدوا إلا إياه )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's promise to provide children first answers the fear parents cannot provide; their priority contrasts with 6:151, where parents are named first.
rows.anchor: نحن نرزقهم وإياكم ( ضمان لرزقهم

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: Shaykh al-Islam explains the contrast with 6:151 by present poverty there versus anticipated poverty here, so children are named first here.
rows.anchor: لأن الباعث على القتل هناك الإملاق الناجز ولذلك قيل من إملاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling child-killing a great خطء also explains the prohibition: it cuts off descendants and human continuity.
rows.anchor: تعليل آخر ببيان أن المنهي عنه في نفسه منكر عظيم لما فيه من قطع التناسل

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن ذكوان عن عامر
rows.claim: Abu Ja'far and Ibn Dhakwan from Amir read خطأ with fatḥa on خاء and طاء and no length; al-Zajjaj parses it as a verbal noun or a dialect word for sin.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو جعفر وابن ذكوان عن عامر ( خطأ )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The objection that خطأ means an unintentional mistake and cannot fit deliberate killing shows a lack of linguistic knowledge.
rows.anchor: فمن استشكل هذه القراءة بأن الخطأ ما لم يتعمد وليس هذا محله

rows.speaker: ابن كثير
rows.claim: Ibn Kathir reads خطاء with kasra, fatḥa, and length; it may be a dialect form of خطء meaning sin, or a verbal noun of خاطأ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ( خطاء )

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu Ali says خاطأ is supported by the attested reciprocal verb تخطأ in a line describing a hunter's arrow missing a truffle.
rows.anchor: قال أبو علي الفارسي : وإن كنا لم نجد خاطأ لكن وجد تخطأ مطاوعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that derivation, the verse means child-killing departs from right and sound judgment, so Abu Hatim was wrong to call the reading erroneous.
rows.anchor: والمعنى على هذا إن قتلهم كان عدو لا عن الحق والصواب

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hasan reads خطاء with fatḥa and length, treating it as a verbal noun from أخطأ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن ( خطاء ) بفتح الخاء والطاء مع المد

rows.speaker: الزهري وأبو رجاء وابن عامر
rows.claim: Al-Zuhri and Abu Raja read خطا with a final alif replacing hamza; another narration from Ibn Amir reads it like عصا.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الزهري وأبو رجاء ( خطا ) بكسر الخاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not even approach zina: the command bars near and distant preliminaries as well as the act itself, since approaching leads to committing it.
rows.anchor: بمباشرة مباديه القريبة أو البعيدة فضلا عن مباشرته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording is more emphatic than nearby prohibitions because it forbids proximity to zina itself and approach leads toward the act.
rows.anchor: والنهي عن قربانه على خلاف ما سبق ولحق للمبالغة في النهي عن نفسه

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib defines zina as intercourse without a lawful marriage contract; the noun occurs in both long and shortened forms.
rows.anchor: وفسره الراغب بوطء المرأة من غير عقد شرعي وجاء فيه المد والقصر

rows.speaker: شيخ الإسلام
rows.claim: Shaykh al-Islam says the verse falls between child-killing and killing a protected soul because zina destroys lineage, making an unestablished lineage like death in law.
rows.anchor: كما قال شيخ الإسلام باعتبار أنه قتل للأولاد لما أنه تضييع للأنساب
